newsitem.title: USA: NRC tells Maine Yankee to improve "safety culture".
newsitem.headline: NRC tells Maine Yankee to improve "safety culture".

text.p: Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials warned Tuesday they will be closely watching to see if the troubled Maine Yankee nuclear plant adopts a new "safety culture."

Maine Yankee and NRC officials met at the 910-megawatt facility to discuss the plant's response to 16 alleged safety violations uncovered in a recent inspection and why those and other problems were allowed to develop.
"I don't know how to guage sincerity ... we will make the judgement based on what we see in the way of results," NRC regional director Hubert Miller told reporters after the three-hour meeting.

Investigations conducted last year by the NRC and plant concluded that Maine Yankee had adopted a corporate culture that discouraged workers from exposing potential safety problems because managers wanted to keep operating costs low.
Maine Yankee president Mike Sellman, who assumed his post last month, acknowledged the plant has not done enough to address safety concerns but vowed that the situation was improving.

"You've been in the driver's seat (on safety). It's time for us to sit there," Sellman said, promising that Maine Yankee would adopt a "safety culture strong enough to be self-critical and self-healing."
Sellman is an employee of Entergy Corp., which was contracted by Maine Yankee's directors to provide management services after nearly two years of shutdowns and safety gaffes at the plant.

Miller said that because of past management problems he expected there would be an increase in the number of reported problems, but an increase in complaints would also show workers are concerned about safety.
"Part of guaging results will be seeing if there is actually an increase in the number of problems that are being reported," Miller told reporters.

Maine Yankee has been off-line since Dec 6 while workers fix problems with misrouted electric cables and leaking fuel rods. The steam generator will also be inspected for potential tube cracking problems.

The 24-year-old facility, once considered by regulators to be among the safest in the U.S., is not expected to return to operation until late summer at the earliest and will need NRC approval before restarting.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
